body: Depth: Nifty Smallcap 250 TRI calendar-year falls: 2008 -73% (Nifty 50 TRI -59%), 2018 -36% (-14%), 2020 -43% (-38%), 2025 -24% (-8%) (DSP). Nifty Smallcap 100 maximum intra-year falls: 76% (2008), 47% (2020), 40% (2018), 33% (2022), 23% (2025); a fall of at least 10% occurred in 21 of 22 calendar years 2004-2025 (5paisa). Frequency: intra-year falls over 20% happened 12 times in 2005-2025 for Smallcap 250 TRI vs 4 times for the Nifty 50 TRI - roughly every 2 years vs every 5. Time underwater: from Jan 2004 to Sep 2026 the Smallcap 100 spent 63% of trading days >10% below its peak, 45% >20% below and 36% >30% below (Sensex: 33%, 11%, 4%). Recovery to prior peak: after 2008 >6 years (Smallcap 250 TRI) or ~69 months to Nov 2014 for the Smallcap 100 (BSE Smallcap ~2017 on closes); after 2018 ~3 years; after the 2024 peak, still below 18 months later (Mar 2026). Rule of thumb: a 30-40% smallcap fall is normal and takes ~2-3 years to recover; a 60-75% fall after a valuation bubble takes 5-7 years. Implication: size smallcap allocations so that a 50% fall is survivable financially and psychologically; staggered buying during drawdowns earns most of the excess return (Rs 1 lakh at the 2008 bottom ~18% CAGR vs ~8% from the pre-crisis peak).
title: How deep and how long Indian smallcap drawdowns last
